library: Prairie Avenue 1904 K03 brick library - profiles
read_by: T-2291 (the K03 wall on a named target) and every Prairie component that builds brick
rule: Joints, bonds, specials and firing spread are DATA here, in metres. No fabric map carries a joint; a component builds them from this file at full detail, and the lod panels are rendered from it for the balanced and light exports.

module.why: the Glessner v4 brick module (generators/archetypes/masonry_house_v4_detail.py), so every brick in the district registers with the canonical asset; each fabric's joint comes out of the module rather than being added to it
module.confidence: reconstructed - no 1904 brick size for these houses is a source here

condition: Clean 1904 bodies. Soot, damp, efflorescence and dirt are condition masks laid over the fabric (T-2291), never baked into it, so body clay and dirt stay separable.

pressed_red.variation_rule: each unit draws ONE variant by weight, independently, from a generator seeded by (component seed, course, unit): no alternating, banded or checkerboard pattern, and the same wall draws the same bricks on every machine (K01 § seed)

uses.register: Pressed dark-red brick with tight dark joints, contrasting sandstone bands
Five-bay red-brick front, pale marble trim and belts

pressed_red.not_for: service walls, party walls and rear ranges (common_buff), or any front the register gives to stone
pressed_red.note: Dry-pressed face brick: a dense, smooth, even red face with crisp arrises, a faint press sheen and only fine pinholes; laid with thin dark joints so the wall reads as one colour field. Body colour and burn spread are reconstructed.

common_buff.variation_rule: each unit draws ONE variant by weight, independently, from a generator seeded by (component seed, course, unit): no alternating, banded or checkerboard pattern, and the same wall draws the same bricks on every machine (K01 § seed)

uses.register: Smooth ashlar street face, common-brick returns
Brownstone walls and brick service range

common_buff.not_for: a street front the register names as pressed or rough brick
common_buff.note: Common (service) brick for returns, party walls, rear ranges and coach houses: a sandy buff-to-salmon body, softer arrises, sand and lime specks, wider struck joints and a broader firing spread than a face brick. Colour and spread are reconstructed, kept in the Glessner v4 common brick's grey-tan family.

dark_fired.variation_rule: each unit draws ONE variant by weight, independently, from a generator seeded by (component seed, course, unit): no alternating, banded or checkerboard pattern, and the same wall draws the same bricks on every machine (K01 § seed)

uses.register: the study's 'dark fired variants' (ASSET-CATALOG K03): an accent unit, not a wall fabric

dark_fired.not_for: a whole wall; it is the header of a Flemish front or a single course, and no register entry yet names one
dark_fired.note: Overburnt, kiln-end brick: purple-brown to near-black, partly vitrified with glassy specks and small bloats. Offered as the header of a Flemish bond and nowhere else until a house's evidence asks for it.

rough_red_brown.variation_rule: each unit draws ONE variant by weight, independently, from a generator seeded by (component seed, course, unit): no alternating, banded or checkerboard pattern, and the same wall draws the same bricks on every machine (K01 § seed)
rough_red_brown.not_for: any front other than one the register calls rough; its chipped arris is Mayer's, not a general weathering
rough_red_brown.note: Rough-faced red-brown brick: a torn, dragged face with pits and grit, irregular chipped arrises and deep raked joints that put a shadow under every course. Colour, tear and chip rate are reconstructed.

mortar_dark.note: Fine dark-tinted mortar for tight pressed-brick joints: a lime-and-sand putty darkened to read with a dark red face. The tint is reconstructed; the register's Sherman entry asks for 'tight dark joints' and names no recipe.

mortar_lime.note: Sandy lime mortar for common and rough brick: warm grey-cream with visible sand and the odd lime nodule, the Glessner v4 mortar's family at the brick library's scale. Clean 1904 condition; soot and damp are condition masks (T-2291), not this map.

flush.description: struck off flush with the face; a thin flat line barely behind the arrises

struck.description: pressed back at the bottom, flush at the top: a ledge on the brick below catches water

weathered.description: pressed back at the top, flush at the bottom: sloped to shed water off the brick below

raked.description: raked out square to a uniform depth, so each course casts a shadow line

running.description: stretcher (running) bond: every unit a stretcher, each course offset half a module

common_6.description: common (American) bond: five stretcher courses, then a header course tying the wythes

flemish.description: Flemish bond: stretcher and header alternate in every course, each header centred on the stretcher below

header.face: bed depth x height, set across the wall to tie the wythes
header.note: the header's face is a half module so it registers with the stretcher joints

soldier.face: height x length, stood on end
soldier.width_m: course x 1.5 - joint, rounded to the bond
soldier.use: a flat head over an opening or a band; reads the bond's module, never a free width

rowlock.face: height x bed depth, on edge
rowlock.use: segmental and round arch rings, sills and the cap of a garden wall

segmental_arch.taper: the bricks stay rectangular and the JOINT wedges: joint at the intrados is the fabric's joint width, at the extrados it opens to whatever closes the ring, capped at 2.5 x the joint width; past that add a ring
segmental_arch.keystone: none in brick unless the house's evidence shows one

jack_arch.taper: joints fan from a common centre below the opening
jack_arch.use: flat heads where the register calls for them

string_course.rule: projects from the wall plane; its top is weathered (sloped) so it sheds water. A band in a different fabric is the house's call (sandstone and marble belts are K02's)

corner_return.rule: the bond turns the corner unbroken: a course that ends in a stretcher on one face starts with a header-length return on the other, so the half-module offset continues round the quoin. Flemish and common-bond header courses take a queen closer (a quarter-module cut) beside the quoin header

panels.for: a pressed-brick street front (Sherman-type) at the balanced and light exports
